post.description:
Creates a transaction that converts fiat to a digital asset.

Where the converted asset is delivered depends on whether you send `wallet_address`:

- **Include `wallet_address`** — the asset is sent to that address on the network you specify. Use this when each customer holds their own wallet.
- **Omit `wallet_address`** — the asset is credited to your Ramp merchant custodial wallet, and you credit the customer on your own ledger. Use this when you hold balances for your customers.

The `merchant_reference` must be unique. Reusing one returns a duplicate transaction error.

merchant_reference.description: Your unique reference for this transaction.

wallet_address.description: Where the converted asset is delivered. Omit this object entirely to have the asset credited to your merchant custodial wallet instead. Sending it empty or partially filled is not the same as omitting it.

address.description: Destination wallet address. Validate it before calling this endpoint.

put.description: Recalculates the quote on a transaction that has not been confirmed, and optionally changes the amount. Call this if the customer takes longer than the quote window to proceed.

value.message: Currency swap not allowed: ngn -> usdtg

post.description:
Locks the quote and generates a single-use bank account for the customer's deposit. This request takes no body.

The customer must transfer exactly `amount_expected`, which is the transaction amount plus the processor fee and VAT. Deposits above or below that amount are rejected. The name on the paying account must match the customer name on the transaction, because third-party deposits are not supported.

Note that `data.reference` here is the **bank account** reference (`BANK_ACCOUNT_...`), not the transaction reference. Store it separately — overwriting the `TRX-...` reference from the create response breaks transaction lookups.

Only confirm when the customer is ready to pay.

reference.description: Reference for the generated bank account. This is not the transaction reference — do not overwrite the `TRX-...` value with it.

amount_expected.description: Exact total the customer must transfer, including the processor fee and VAT.

vat.description: VAT charged on the processor fee.

post.description:
Requests a GHS mobile money debit against an on-ramp transaction you have already created.

The response carries `next_step`, which tells you how the customer authorises the debit:

- `OTP` — the provider sends a one-time code. Collect it and call **Verify a mobile money OTP**.
- `PIN` — the provider pushes a prompt to the customer's handset. They approve it there and you take no further action.

Call this endpoint again to send the customer a new code. There is no cap on resends.

next_step.description: How the customer authorises the debit.

instruction.description: Prompt you can show the customer. The wording differs between OTP and PIN.
instruction.example: You will receive a prompt on your mobile number ******7778 to enter your PIN to authorize your payment request of GHS 1000

data.instruction: You will receive a prompt on your mobile number ******7778 to enter your PIN to authorize your payment request of GHS 1000

400.description: The deposit could not be initiated.

post.description:
Submits the one-time code the provider sent to the customer. Only call this when `next_step` was `OTP`.

This endpoint is idempotent, so a customer can submit a code more than once for the same transaction without it being charged twice. If the code expires, initiate the deposit again to send a new one.

otp.description: The code the provider sent to the customer.

400.description: The code could not be verified.

value.message: Failed to verify the OTP for your mobile money deposit. Please try again.

get.description:
Creates a **static** NGN bank account tied to one customer. Any fiat sent to it is converted automatically and delivered to the wallet address you registered, with no per-transaction API call.

Use this for recurring funding, where a customer keeps their own account details. For one-off purchases, use the standard on-ramp flow, which issues a single-use account per transaction.

Static accounts are available for NGN on request and require the customer's BVN.

bank_account.description: Details needed to open the static account.

bank_code.description: Bank the static account is opened with. `035` is Wema Bank.

post.description:
Creates a transaction that converts a digital asset to fiat and pays it to the customer's bank or mobile money account.

The amount of the asset you send determines the fiat the customer receives. The `merchant_reference` must be unique.

from_amount.description: Amount of the asset the customer is selling.

put.description: Recalculates the quote before the customer sends the asset. Use the same `merchant_reference` you used to create the transaction.

post.description:
Attaches the bank or mobile money account that will receive the fiat payout.

Ramp resolves the account and compares the resolved name against the customer name on the transaction. If they do not match, the account is not attached. Add the payout account before confirming the transaction.

account_number.description: The customer's bank account number, or their mobile money number for GHS.

200.description: Bank account successfully created and attached.

example.message: Bank account successfully created and attached to off-ramp transaction

400.description: The account could not be attached.

post.description:
Generates the deposit address the customer sends the asset to.

The customer must send the exact amount, in the correct asset, on the correct network. Anything else may fail or need manual review. Confirm only after the payout account has been attached.

address.description: Where the customer sends the asset.

tag.description: Destination tag or memo. Null on networks that do not use one.

get.description:
Returns the current state of an on-ramp transaction, including the fiat deposit and the crypto payout.

Pass the Quidax `reference` returned when the transaction was created, not your own `merchant_reference`.
Returns the current state of an off-ramp transaction, including the crypto deposit and the fiat payout.
Returns a paginated list of on-ramp transactions for the authenticated app. Use the date filters for reconciliation runs.

value.message: start_date and end_date must both be present
page must be a positive integer

get.description:
Returns the banks and mobile money providers supported in a country. Use each entry's `code` as the `bank_code` when adding a payout account or submitting refund details.

Fetch this list rather than hard-coding it, so newly supported institutions reach your integration without a release.

post.description:
Resolves a bank account and returns the account holder's name. Call this before submitting refund details, so you can confirm the destination with your customer. A completed refund cannot be reversed.

A failed verification returns `400` immediately.

Submits the account that should receive a refund, in response to a `buy_transaction.refund.details_requested` webhook.

Submitting identical details more than once in the same refund cycle is safe. Ramp stores one submission and returns the refund.

get.description: Returns the refund attached to an on-ramp transaction. Use this to reconcile if you miss a refund webhook.

404.description: The refund could not be found.
